must_fix.what: A damaged session file now stops the start. destination() runs `row.get('library') in {set}`, so a LibraryTab row whose 'library' is a list or an object raises TypeError: unhashable type. The call is reached through waits() in the loop condition of restore_rows, which is outside the try/except. Session's cleaner checks 'device', 'group', 'path' and other keys, but not the new 'library', 'folder' or 'title'. The window is never built, launch.py shows its failure message, and every later start reads the same file. Part A fixed this same fault for 'target' and the settings place (test_a_saved_target_or_settings_place_that_is_not_text_is_the_default). Fix: in destination(), use `isinstance(row.get('library'),str) and row['library'] in ...`, and/or have the Session cleaner keep only text in 'library', 'folder' and 'title'. Add the case to the damaged-values test.

must_fix.what: name() builds on-screen words from the class name when a row has no 'title'. Every row a 0.8.3 session wrote has no title, so this is what the owner sees at the first 0.8.4 start. A StacyFoundationTab row then shows as 'Stacy foundation' in two places: the new Activity line ('Not reopened at start · Stacy foundation (five pins were already open) ...') and the labels of Arrange → Reopen deferred tabs. That breaks the one-name rule (one agent, Kasandra; the internal name never shows). On screen the tab is called 'Graphite · knowledge'. The patch's CODE_KEPT entry in tools/name_sweep.py excuses the literal as 'a class name: the kind a saved tab is written down with', but this code shows it to the owner. Fix: give a kind with no title its on-screen name (a small map, or the navigator's label for the NAVIGATION key), never words made from a class name that holds the internal name. Add such a row to a test.

Start time now grows with the rooms left open. With 16 rooms open, the second start took 7.06 s against 5.00 s with nothing open (offscreen, nice 19, shared 4-core machine, one run each, so this is rough). The rooms' constructors make kernel reads at start, and these go into the Activity journal: changes.workspaces, work.list, assignments.list, workers.status, exchange.identity. When a background service is attached and does not answer, the Service details panel adds its 2 s rpc timeout. This is the same cost as opening the rooms by hand, but nothing measures it.

summary: The patch does what the item asked, and its tests are real. The desk's rooms, the app rooms, the navigation's tabs, Service details, This computer and Pills now reopen at start, in order, with Files in its folder and the Library on its kind. Reopen deferred tabs holds each tab once, at most 20. What a start sets aside is said once in the Activity, in words, in both looks. Leaving with Night Shift open no longer loses the session. All counts reproduce: test_session_start 23/23 in both looks; importers test_delete_words 6, test_one_name 19, test_graphite 29 and test_release_check 23 green in both looks; the before-check gives 5 failures and 1 error at HEAD. Four of five reverted pieces turn their tests red. Two small defects must be fixed before merge. (1) A damaged session row whose 'library' is a list or an object now stops the start (TypeError in destination(), outside the try), the fault class Part A just fixed. (2) Rows without a title, which is every row 0.8.3 wrote, are named from class words, so 'Stacy foundation' appears in the Activity line and in the Reopen list. That breaks the one-name rule, and the CODE_KEPT reason does not hold. Both are one-line fixes plus a test case. The rest is should-fix: other names that do not match the screen, an untested told filter, where the Activity line leads when clicked, a silent except, a dead branch, and start time growing with the rooms open.
